summary: A humorous, anecdotal piece on pivotal moments in small and medium enterprise (SME) development, told through fictional entrepreneurs from late 2023 to early 2024. Each vignette covers a stage: inspiration, prototyping, branding, investor pitches, marketing, customer service, scaling, publicity, tech glitches and money management. It deliberately ends without a formal conclusion, stressing the odd, inventive journey over the destination.
one_line: A comic tour of SME development stages, from idea to growth, illustrated by quirky fictional entrepreneurs and their mishaps.
key_facts: Samantha Sparks found inspiration for her company SoapSaver in late September 2023 while trying to keep her soap from turning slimy; SoapSaver launched a soap dish that drains perfectly.
Jeremy 'Gizmo' Clarkson created the 'UntangleR' tangled-earphone solution from his basement in October 2023, through many comically improbable prototype iterations.
Lisa Lemonmouth, a baker, considered 'Lemon Licks' and 'Pucker Up Pies' before naming her business 'Lemonmouth Delights' in November 2023; her abstract logo resembled a preschool's work.
John Dough of 'Rise-Up Breads' gave an investor pitch one December afternoon that was half stand-up, a quarter mime and a quarter elevator pitch; one investor ducked a flying baguette.
Susie Starshine's eco-friendly glitter 'StarDust' got a viral dance challenge hijacked by her Uncle Bob in a bee costume; the mishap was branded 'Bee the Buzz' and worked wonders.
In January 2024 Michael and his 'TechRescue' crew learned about customer satisfaction after their software, promising to 'make your computer woes disappear', failed to do so.
Amy Applebaum's 'Plantable Pencils' became too popular in February 2024; demand outstripped production, and she spent a night at the warehouse planting seeds into pencils.
Phil Flip staged an impromptu marathon in March 2024 where hundreds of runners wore his 'FlipFit Flops', attracting public attention and a flock of seagulls.

Betty of 'BeGone', an organic pest control firm, launched an eco-friendly app in April 2024 billed as bug-free, but a glitch sent false pest alerts and she had to convince clients there was no locust swarm.
Carl Coinworthy's penny-farthing bike café 'Cycle Sip' illustrates money management: he must choose between an ornate coffee machine and practical necessities.
The article's conclusion section declines to conclude, with Holly Hindsight cited as saying there is a method to the madness.
